results.fork: which version of the source dataset is loaded?
results.option: load the raw, unfiltered player-referee dyad dataset
results.note: All record loading the raw, unfiltered player-referee dyad CSV as the analysis base.

results.fork: is the adjusted analysis stratified by position subgroup, and at what granularity?
results.option: stratify the adjusted analysis by position subgroup
results.note: all three re-run the adjusted model separately within each position subgroup

results.fork: Is an unadjusted estimate reported alongside the adjusted one?
results.option: report a crude/unadjusted rate difference alongside the adjusted estimate
results.note: all three report a crude unadjusted rate/risk difference alongside the adjusted estimate

results.fork: how are records with missing covariates handled — complete-case, impute, or recode as explicit category?
results.option: complete-case / listwise deletion
results.note: All record the complete-case/listwise-deletion strategy; variation in which covariates define completeness is a separate decision point.

results.fork: how are records with missing covariates handled — complete-case, impute, or recode as explicit category?
results.option: overall median-impute continuous covariates (height/weight, ±age)
results.note: All record median-imputing missing continuous covariates; weight-only and age-inclusive variants match the option's stated scope.

results.fork: how are records with missing covariates handled — complete-case, impute, or recode as explicit category?
results.option: mean-impute height/weight
results.note: All fill missing height/weight with the sample mean; the 0-on-standardized ones equal mean imputation.

results.fork: How are the primary and sensitivity specifications summarized together?
results.option: assemble comparison table of primary and sensitivity specifications side-by-side
results.note: All three assemble a side-by-side comparison table of primary and sensitivity specs.

results.fork: how are the confidence interval and p-value for the exposure effect computed?
results.option: analytic delta-method SE via g-computation gradient, Wald CI/p

rejects.records: z-test/p using a simulated (Monte Carlo) SE, not a delta-method SE

results.note: one straggler uses a simulated SE; the rest are the same delta-method Wald computation (numerical vs analytic gradient is the same choice)

results.fork: how are the confidence interval and p-value for the exposure effect computed?
results.option: parametric bootstrap from full coefficient MVN/covariance, percentile-quantile inference (percentile CI and crossing-zero p are duals of the same draws)
results.note: All draw coefficients from the model's asymptotic MVN and take percentile inference; draw-count differences don't change the choice.

results.fork: how are the confidence interval and p-value for the exposure effect computed?
results.option: model-based Wald CI/p from the GLM coefficient SE

rejects.records: Wald z p-value built from the bootstrap SE, not the GLM coefficient SE

results.note: one straggler uses bootstrap SE; rest are model-based Wald normal-approx CIs/p-values

results.fork: what fixed reference date is used to compute player age?
results.option: year-only subtraction, fixed 2012 reference year
results.note: all derive age via fixed 2012 reference-year subtraction from birth year

results.fork: what fixed reference date is used to compute player age?
results.option: year-only subtraction, fixed 2013 reference year
results.note: all record age via fixed 2013 reference year minus birth year

results.fork: what fixed reference date is used to compute player age?
results.option: day-based age at fixed 2012-07-01 (mid-2012)
results.note: all five anchor age to the fixed 2012-07-01 mid-season reference date

results.fork: how are non-numeric placeholder / non-finite values coerced to numeric-with-missing during cleaning?
results.option: treat the literal 'NA' string as missing before numeric coercion
results.note: All treat literal 'NA' as missing before numeric coercion; differ only in which variables.

results.fork: which dyads enter the inter-rater reliability check?
results.option: restrict to dyads with both rater1 and rater2 present for the inter-rater reliability check
results.note: all three restrict to dyads with both raters present before reliability check

results.fork: Is the adjustment set expanded by adding covariates as a robustness check?
results.option: robustness: ADD a covariate to the adjustment set
results.note: All record the same choice: expand the adjustment set with extra covariate(s) as a robustness check.

results.fork: how is referee bias controlled for in the model?
results.option: include unspecified referee bias measure(s) as a covariate/block
results.note: all add referee bias measure(s) as covariate/block; option is deliberately measure-agnostic

results.fork: how is referee bias controlled for in the model?
results.option: add referee mean IAT (meanIAT) as a single covariate
results.note: all four add referee mean IAT score as a single adjustment covariate

results.fork: How are bootstrap iterations whose model fit fails handled?
results.option: catch and drop bootstrap iterations whose model fit throws an exception
results.note: all record catching failed model fits and dropping the affected bootstrap iterations

results.fork: how is the skin-tone rating entered as the exposure — continuous or split/binned at which cutpoints?
results.option: enter continuous, raw (per-unit, full range)

rejects.records: rebuilds covariates/sample and re-applies filters, not the continuous exposure-entry choice itself

results.note: one straggler is a sample-prep step; rest all enter skin tone continuous/raw

results.fork: how is the skin-tone rating entered as the exposure — continuous or split/binned at which cutpoints?
results.option: single-cutoff dichotomize at 0.5
results.note: All fourteen dichotomize continuous skin tone into dark/light at the 0.5 midpoint cutoff.

results.fork: how is the skin-tone rating entered as the exposure — continuous or split/binned at which cutpoints?
results.option: drop-middle dichotomize 0.25/0.75
results.note: all drop the middle band and dichotomize light ≤0.25 vs dark ≥0.75

results.fork: how are the per-league values in the forest plot obtained?
results.option: hardcode manually-typed per-league/country OR values instead of computed values (e.g. in forest plot)
results.note: all three hardcode literal per-league/country OR values instead of computed ones

results.fork: Are all skin-tone categories retained, or is the sample collapsed to extreme groups?
results.option: retain all skin-tone categories (no collapsing)

rejects.records: retain all three skin-tone bands (sensitivity check), the only true skin-tone operation here

results.note: Majority (0-3) all record one-hot encoding position/league keeping every level; id 4 is the lone skin-tone choice.

results.fork: Which card events are counted as the outcome event?
results.option: outcome = red cards only (straight reds + second-yellow reds)
results.note: All three define a binary any-red outcome combining straight and second-yellow reds.

results.fork: how is the binary dark-skin exposure variable defined?
results.option: recode an existing light/dark category into a 0/1 binary
results.note: all recode a light/dark skin category into a 0/1 dark-skin exposure indicator

results.fork: which regression model, estimator, and SE scheme specifies the primary confound-adjusted skin-tone effect on red cards?
results.option: log(games) as covariate, no offset
results.note: All 14 record log-transforming games played as a model covariate.

results.fork: which regression model, estimator, and SE scheme specifies the primary confound-adjusted skin-tone effect on red cards?
results.option: LPM (OLS) with cluster-robust SEs
results.note: all ten record LPM/OLS with player-clustered standard errors

results.fork: which regression model, estimator, and SE scheme specifies the primary confound-adjusted skin-tone effect on red cards?
results.option: LPM (OLS) with player-clustered SEs

rejects.records: LPM with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust SEs, not player-clustered SEs

results.note: one straggler uses HC3 robust SEs; rest are player-clustered (or SE unspecified) LPM

results.fork: which regression model and outcome family estimates the exposure–red-card association?
results.option: logistic regression on binary red-card indicator
results.note: All record fitting logistic regression on the binary red-card outcome; wording varies only.

results.fork: which regression model and outcome family estimates the exposure–red-card association?
results.option: Poisson GLM with log(games) offset, plain
results.note: all fit red-card counts via Poisson GLM with a log-games offset; predictor differences are a separate decision

results.fork: which regression model and outcome family estimates the exposure–red-card association?
results.option: plain linear probability model (OLS on binary)
results.note: All three fit an OLS linear-probability model on the binary red-card outcome.

results.fork: at what unit is the dyad-level data aggregated before modeling?
results.option: collapse to one row per player, summing counts
results.note: all three collapse to one row per player by summing counts

results.fork: which covariates does the primary model adjust for (if any)?
results.option: unadjusted, no covariates (crude OR)
results.note: All fit an unadjusted skin-tone-only model; SE/CI variants don't change the no-covariate choice.

results.fork: How is the middle (Medium) skin-tone category handled?
results.option: drop the Medium group, keep only Light and Dark

rejects.records: sensitivity analysis restricting to extreme ratings (0 or 1) only, not merely dropping medium
extreme-groups comparison (<0.25 vs >=0.75) as a refit subsample, drops more than the medium category
sensitivity check on the most extreme tones (0 vs 1.0) only
sensitivity check redefining exposure as very-light/very-dark at 0.25/0.75 thresholds

results.note: Majority drops medium keeping all Light/Dark; four record stricter extreme-groups sensitivity checks selecting different rows

results.fork: how are continuous predictors transformed and z-scored/standardized before modeling?
results.option: z-score a varying subset of continuous covariates (umbrella/aggregate)
results.note: All z-score continuous covariates before modeling; varying covariate subsets match the umbrella/aggregate option.

results.fork: how are continuous predictors transformed and z-scored/standardized before modeling?
results.option: z-score height and weight only
results.note: All record z-scoring height and weight only; wording varies but the operation is identical.

results.fork: how are continuous predictors transformed and z-scored/standardized before modeling?
results.option: z-score raw (unlogged) games, height, and weight
results.note: All record z-standardizing the continuous covariates (games, height, weight) before modeling.

results.fork: are reported effect/plot estimates computed from the data or hardcoded as literal values?
results.option: hard-code reported summary/plot effect estimates as literal values instead of computing them from data
results.note: all record hardcoding reported forest-plot/summary effect estimates as literals instead of computing them

results.fork: Which interaction/moderation term is added to the model?
results.option: generic slope/interaction term with N(0,1) prior
results.note: All add a slope or interaction term with an N(0,1) prior, matching this generic bucket despite differing predictors.
